# r6 — Trustworthy

## What this measures

Agents transact only where identity and integrity are verifiable: OAuth for
identity linking, published signing keys for webhook verification, enforced
TLS, and structured errors an agent can act on instead of an HTML 500 it
can only screenshot.

## Sub-checks

| Sub-check | Pass when | Weight | Fix skill |
|-----------|-----------|-------:|-----------|
| OAuth discovery | `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` → 200 with `issuer` + endpoints | 2 | `ucp-agentic-commerce:ucp-identity-linking` |
| signing keys published | UCP profile carries `signing_keys`/`jwks` | 2 | `ucp-agentic-commerce:ucp-orders-webhooks` |
| HTTPS enforced | `http://` → 301/302/307/308 to `https://` | 1 | — |
| HSTS | `strict-transport-security` header on origin | 1 | — |
| structured errors | malformed POST → 4xx with JSON `{type/error/message}`, not HTML | 1 | `acp-agentic-commerce:acp-dev-patterns` |

## N/A condition

None.

## Fix guidance

OAuth discovery is the gateway to identity linking (guest → recognized
customer), which raises agent conversion more than any other trust item.
Signing keys make your webhooks verifiable — without them a platform cannot
trust an `order.updated` event came from you.
